requirements: |
  Functional Requirements
  FR1: The app must find the latest session by session date that contains the current exercise and at least one executed set.
  FR2: Exercise-name matching must ignore case, diacritics, leading and trailing whitespace, and repeated internal whitespace.
  FR3: The app must recognize the approved legacy aliases Puxada frontal to Puxada frontal pegada neutra, Supino inclinado to Supino inclinado com halteres, Tríceps to Tríceps na corda, and Prancha to Prancha nos antebraços.
  FR4: Names that differ after normalization and are not in the explicit alias map must be treated as a new exercise; fuzzy matching is not allowed.
  FR5: Legacy saved sessions whose sets do not have a confirmation field must be read as records of executed sets.
  FR6: Previous and current sets must be paired by executed-set position: first with first, second with second, and so on.
  FR7: A current set with no corresponding previous executed set must remain empty and be identified as a first execution.
  FR8: When usable history exists, the app must prefill each set's weight and repetitions with the last executed values.
  FR9: Recovered values must be identified in the interface as values from the last execution, not as a recommendation or a completed set.
  FR10: Every prefilled weight and repetition value must remain directly editable; keeping a value must require no re-entry.
  FR11: New saved sets must carry the state that the checkmark confirmed the set as executed.
  FR12: The final session record must contain only sets confirmed with the checkmark.
  FR13: Prefilled but unconfirmed sets must never appear as executed in History, Markdown export, HTML export, sharing, or printing.
  FR14: Confirming a set with the checkmark must update its visible state and immediately start that exercise's configured rest when automatic rest is enabled and the rest is greater than zero.
  FR15: Unconfirming a set must preserve the entered values and must not silently cancel a rest timer that has already started.
  FR16: The app must show a progression notice only when every executed set in the latest execution reached the numeric upper bound of a numeric planned repetition range.
  FR17: The progression notice must not appear for nonnumeric or unusable repetition data and must never change the weight field automatically.
  FR18: After ten saved sessions without an export, the app must show an export reminder immediately after session save and never during a workout; the app must retain when the last export occurred.
  FR19: Phase 2 must present one exercise at a time while keeping the timer panel available.
  FR20: Phase 2 must provide explicit Skip and Back actions and visible In progress, Pending, Partial, and Completed states.
  FR21: Skipping, returning, or moving between exercises must preserve every value and confirmation entered in the current session.
  FR22: Phase 2 must save a local session draft after each edit, confirmation, unconfirmation, skip, and return.
  FR23: When an interrupted draft exists, the app must offer explicit Continue workout and Discard draft actions.
  FR24: Confirming the last set of an exercise must start the normal rest, advance to the next exercise, show a short completion message, and retain an explicit Back action.
  FR25: Before final save, the app must summarize Completed, Partial, and Pending exercises and offer Return to workout or Save as partial when work remains.
  FR26: A draft must not enter History; only the existing explicit final session-save action may create the final history record.
  FR27: The existing Not trained flow, readiness controls, sleep, energy, pain, body weight, notes, complete History, exports, sharing, printing, and delete behavior must remain available.
  FR28: Workout and rest timers must remain visible, accurate, and uninterrupted while navigating between exercises and tabs.
  FR29: The feature must not add a tutorial, welcome screen, hidden gesture, or version announcement.
  FR30: Phase 3 must modernize the five tabs and fixed timer panel through color, typography, hierarchy, and spacing while retaining the dark theme, explicit actions, and all current capabilities.

  Non-Functional Requirements
  NFR1: Core workout, history, draft, prefill, confirmation, navigation, and timer behavior must work without a network connection.
  NFR2: Workout data must remain on the device; the feature must add no server, analytics, account, login, or tracking.
  NFR3: Chrome on an Android phone, served over HTTP or HTTPS, is the mandatory validation target because that browser holds the production history.
  NFR4: Desktop browsers remain a secondary target and must not receive a different workflow or become required for any action.
  NFR5: The interface must be designed first for portrait touch use with one hand, large targets, short reading, and short typing.
  NFR6: No touch target may become smaller than its current equivalent.
  NFR7: No text may have lower contrast than its current equivalent, and no currently visible information may depend on a hidden gesture or an unlabeled icon.
  NFR8: Exercise and set state must be communicated with text or symbols as well as color.
  NFR9: Historical values must appear without perceptible delay, blank-state flash, or intermediate redraw when the workout logger opens.
  NFR10: Historical lookup must run when the workout day is assembled and must not be repeated on every keystroke.
  NFR11: Checkmark feedback and automatic rest start must remain immediate.

content.text:
Registro completo do `epics.md` na mão. Agora a análise, antes de eu escrever qualquer linha.

## O que o Passo 9 faz e por que ele é sério

Esta seção é o **contrato de capacidades** do produto. A regra do método é dura: *quem desenha a UX só desenha o que estiver aqui; quem faz a arquitetura só sustenta o que estiver aqui; as tarefas de implementação só constroem o que estiver aqui.* Uma capacidade que não entrar nesta lista não existirá no produto final.

## O problema: já existem duas numerações de FR neste projeto

| | Rascunho `_fr.md` | Registro do `epics.md` |
|---|---|---|
| **Quantos** | FR1 a FR49 | FR1 a FR30 (+ NFR1–15, AR1–13) |
| **Idioma** | pt-BR | inglês |
| **Está dentro do PRD?** | Não — arquivo solto | Não — mas é o registro aprovado |
| **Quem usa** | ninguém | `epics.md`, relatório de prontidão, as 6 specs de `epic-1`, e os critérios de aceite do próprio issue |
| **Granularidade** | cada preservação é um FR próprio (cronômetro, som, exportação, offline…) | preservação condensada em **um** FR27 + os NFRs |

O detalhe que decide: o critério de aceite do `epic-1`, escrito por você, diz **"FR1 through FR18"**. No registro de 30, FR1–FR18 é exatamente a Fase 1. No rascunho de 49, FR1–FR18 seria outra coisa completamente. Ou seja, a numeração viva é a do `epics.md`.

## As três saídas

**1. Adotar o registro do `epics.md` (FR1–FR30).** O PRD passa a falar a mesma língua das specs já liberadas. Nada quebra. Preço: as capacidades preservadas ficam agrupadas no FR27 em vez de terem um número cada.

**2. Adotar o rascunho `_fr.md` (FR1–FR49).** Mais detalhado, cada preservação vira um requisito conferível. Preço: quebra a numeração de **tudo** que já está aprovado — as 6 specs, o `epics.md` e o relatório de prontidão precisariam ser renumerados, e isso não é trabalho deste workflow.

**3. FR1–FR30 e acrescentar as preservações como FR31 em diante.** Nada quebra e a granularidade volta. Preço: os FR31+ nasceriam sem cobertura em nenhum epic, o que aparece como buraco na próxima checagem de prontidão.

**Minha recomendação é a 1.** O PRD está chegando atrasado a uma festa onde o registro já foi reconciliado e aprovado, e o EPIC-1 já está liberado para implementação. O papel do PRD agora é ficar consistente com o contrato aprovado, não criar uma terceira numeração. E a granularidade não se perde de verdade: as seções em prosa do PRD já descrevem cada item de preservação em detalhe.

---

**Selecione:** `[1] Adotar FR1–FR30 do epics.md` `[2] Adotar FR1–FR49 do _fr.md` `[3] FR1–FR30 mais preservações como FR31+`
